title: Partition-wise Graph Filtering: A Unified Perspective Through the Lens of Graph Coarsening

problem.claim: Uniform graph-wise filtering struggles with heterophilic graphs, while node-wise filtering introduces excessive parameterization and potential overfitting risks.

gap.claim: A comprehensive framework unifying graph-wise and node-wise filtering is absent, limiting theoretical insight into these paradigms.

contributions.claim: The paper analyzes graph-wise and node-wise filtering through the Contextual Stochastic Block Model and identifies a sufficient synthesis for classification on graphs with both homophily and heterophily.
The paper introduces Coarsening-guided Partition-wise Filtering, which filters node partitions rather than applying only graph-wise or node-wise filtering.
CPF combines structure-aware filtering over graph-coarsening partitions with feature-aware filtering over k-means feature clusters to refine node embeddings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their analysis shows CPF is superior to other filtering paradigms.
The authors report validation through benchmark node-classification experiments and a real-world graph-anomaly-detection application.
The authors report that code is available in a GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Filtering-based GNNs use graph filters for graph-structured data and have succeeded across graph-related tasks.
Graph-wise filtering applies one uniform filter and struggles with heterophily; node-wise filtering improves adaptability but raises parameterization and overfitting concerns.
Existing strategies lack a comprehensive unifying framework.
CPF addresses the gap by filtering structure-aware and feature-aware node partitions.
The paper reports analytical comparisons, benchmark classification experiments, and a graph anomaly-detection application.

source_observation.claim: The abstract describes filtering over partitions formed from graph structure and node features.

interpretation.claim: Intermediate-granularity parameter sharing may balance the adaptability of node-wise filtering with the regularization of graph-wise filtering.

application.claim: When designing graph-filtering systems, consider structure- and feature-based partitions as a way to localize filtering without assigning a separate filter to every node.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when partition-wise filtering fails or how its computational and statistical trade-offs compare across graph regimes.

unknowns: Specific benchmark datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not provided.
Theoretical assumptions and proof details are not provided.
Partitioning costs, hyperparameters, and ablation results are not provided.
